headline: Next polls under a caretaker government, says Home Minister
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed confirms the restoration of the caretaker system through a constitutional amendment to ensure fair elections.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed announced that the next national election will be held under a caretaker government, stating that a political consensus has already been reached on the issue.
The restoration of the system will be achieved through a constitutional amendment, as the government is committed to fulfilling one of the primary demands of the recent movement.
Referring to the Supreme Court's decision, the minister noted that the court had judicially revived the caretaker system by overturning a previous judgement by Justice Khairul Haque.
On other matters, Salahuddin Ahmed addressed reports regarding the former prime minister Sheikh Hasina's potential return to Bangladesh in December, stating the government is aware of the claims.
He revealed that Bangladesh has sent several requests to India through the foreign ministry seeking her return under the extradition treaty.
The Home Minister also confirmed that law and order in Sajek has been brought under control following internal disputes among various local groups during the tourism season.

Regarding allegations against an additional deputy inspector general of police, the minister stated the officer has been attached and departmental proceedings will be initiated following legal procedures.
caption:
The next national election will be held under a caretaker government.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed confirms the system will be restored via constitutional amendment.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed announced that the next national election will be held under a caretaker government, stating that a political consensus has already been reached on the issue.

The restoration of the system will be achieved through a constitutional amendment, as the government is committed to fulfilling one of the primary demands of the recent movement.

Referring to the Supreme Court's decision, the minister noted that the court had judicially revived the caretaker system by overturning a previous judgement by Justice Khairul Haque.

On other matters, Salahuddin Ahmed addressed reports regarding the former prime minister Sheikh Hasina's potential return to Bangladesh in December, stating the government is aware of the claims.

He revealed that Bangladesh has sent several requests to India through the foreign ministry seeking her return under the extradition treaty.

The Home Minister also confirmed that law and order in Sajek has been brought under control following internal disputes among various local groups during the tourism season.

Regarding allegations against an additional deputy inspector general of police, the minister stated the officer has been attached and departmental proceedings will be initiated following legal procedures.

headline_marked: PM Tarique Rahman [[arrives in Tokyo for 4-day state visit]] to Japan
headline: PM Tarique Rahman arrives in Tokyo for 4-day state visit to Japan
summary: The visit aims to deepen bilateral ties, attract fresh Japanese investment, and expand trade and development cooperation.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman reached Tokyo this morning on a four-day official visit at the invitation of Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. He was received at Narita International Airport by Japanese State Minister for Foreign Affairs Yasutaka Nakasone.
Tarique Rahman is scheduled to hold high-level bilateral talks with the Japanese prime minister on October 27, followed by a joint press announcement and a luncheon.
During the visit, the prime minister will meet Japanese government officials, development institutions, and business leaders, and deliver the keynote address at the Bangladesh-Japan Economic Forum.

The visit is expected to attract fresh Japanese investment and accelerate ongoing development projects, including the implementation of the Bangladesh-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement signed in February 2026.

Discussions will focus on renewable energy, agriculture, science and technology, digital transformation, and human resource development. Around eight MoUs are under discussion, with three to four likely to be signed.
The prime minister's itinerary includes visits to an LNG terminal and power plant in Futtsu City, the headquarters of UNIQLO, and a Toyota factory in Nagoya.
The two sides will also discuss regional peace, a sustainable solution to the Rohingya crisis, and cooperation in addressing the energy crisis.

Japan has been a major development partner for Bangladesh since 1972, supporting key infrastructure projects like the Dhaka metro rail and the third terminal of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport.
